title: PLAN — SB-072: migration — every placeholder family onto the road as marked stubs

context.setupNotes:
Markup and compiler work happens in this checkout (design-lab). Godot code, generated .tres and GATH work happen in ../lifelines-core-loop. Run pm only from the design-lab checkout.

## The migration law (applies to every task)
1. Copy the legacy text VERBATIM into markup, block marked `Stub: yes`. Agents never author or improve prose — Terje rewrites the stubs later in the gate session (SB-073). Byte-identical means byte-identical: keep typos, casing, punctuation.
2. Compile: `npm run gen:content` (design-lab) writes the slice JSON and per-character sim-content JSON into core-loop.
3. Generate: `/Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --headless --path ../lifelines-core-loop --script res://scripts/case_files/generate_sim_content.gd` (visits ride the case pack generator, see docs/case-content-runtime.md). Commit the generated .tres.
4. Prove the round-trip: a GATH fixture test compares the generated resource text against the legacy literal captured BEFORE deletion (PLAN-006's OPPDRAG_BEATS verbatim fixture is the precedent). Red-green verify per tests/README.md.
5. Delete the legacy const / hand-edited file / fallback path IN THE SAME STEP. Sparse-field law: presence of a generated resource = cutover, so a green suite with the const still present proves nothing — the fallback serves identical text. Every proof must assert (a) the generated resource exists, (b) the legacy source is gone, (c) text matches the fixture.
6. GATH green: `/Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --headless --path ../lifelines-core-loop -s tests/runner.gd`. Design-lab side: `npm run case:check` and `npm test`.

## Scope rulings that bind this plan
- DD-004: the UI-chrome/scene text layer stays OUT (own later SDD). Narrow exception: divergent duplicates that shadow a migrated family die in this wave — raw frank-action navn literals, the håndbok category words that live in 3 places, and the SI FRA vs HEVDE SEG class collapse to one source.
- SB-072 amendments (ticket comment): sibling files are IN (frank_action_handlers, report_composer, tiltak_visit_director, tiltak_dawn_handlers, case_engine/case_host stray lines); the 20 dead prologue mail strings are DELETED, not migrated (household_object_manager discards the payload today — preserve that behavior).
- Done-ness extent = the SB-064 inventory checklist (eight families + siblings, counts per family in that ticket's comment) with the three amendments.

## Sequencing-law flip (planned, not a deviation)
PLAN-008 deliberately kept `SimContentGenerator.regenerate_default()` from writing thought pools while the 15 hand-edited resources/thoughts/*.tres stayed production. Task 2 flips that: enable thoughts in the default run and delete the hand-edited files in the same step. PLAN-008's own comments name SB-072 as the owner of this flip.

## Fallback-gap bookkeeping
PLAN-008 intended each surviving fallback const as a named pm gap; none is visible in either store today. Task 7 hunts both pm stores and PLAN-008 task notes, and closes or files-and-closes whatever bookkeeping exists so no stale 'const survives' record outlives this plan.

## Implementation slices
Slice 1 — character content on the built road: Tasks 1–2 (barks/phone prove the recipe, then thoughts + MTG fold).
Slice 2 — visit content: Task 3.
Slice 3 — StringTable families (first runtime consumers get wired here): Tasks 4–6.
Slice 4 — done-ness sweep: Task 7.
Tasks are chained serially: sim.md files recur across 1–2, tiny-olsen.case.md recurs across 3–6, and the one-family-per-step law wants settled ground between cutovers.
designDecisions: Every migrated block carries `Stub: yes`; stub marking survives compile into the runtime resource (SDD-130 §2). The seed-skeleton demo blocks in the sim.md files (PLAN-006 TASK-028) are replaced by the real migrated content, not kept alongside it.

`# Strings:` blocks live in content/cases/olsen/tiny-olsen.case.md — that is the built road (CaseSlice sparse `strings` key → StringTable .tres under resources/cases/olsen/generated/strings/). One block per family id: notat, prologue, handbok, tiltak, frank_actions (executor may adjust ids; flat by design, no nesting).

StringTable becomes the SOLE runtime text home for notat/håndbok/prologue copy. The håndbok tiltak/frank_actions .tres keep their data fields (costs, krav predicates), but their text fields stop being authoritative — overlay-at-load from the StringTable or lookup-at-display, executor's choice, exactly ONE mechanism. Leaving live duplicate text fields in the .tres plants the drift this SDD exists to kill.

BARK_TEXTS is one global 8-line pool; BarkPool is per character. The 8 lines land verbatim in each conversation-capable character's `# Barks:` pool so every speaker's candidate set is unchanged (byte-identical extends to selection behavior).
Grete's thought-pool asymmetry (no need_hunger, need_social, relational_elling) migrates AS-IS. No new pools, no invented prose — missing pools are Terje's to write in the gate session.

MTG ambient fold (SDD-130 §4): the AMBIENT_POOLS icon keys move into wildcard `# Thoughts` pools per character according to color identity (Elling Blue/Green, Grete White), thought_bubble_manager reads pools instead of the const, and the const dies. SB-505's probe question about ambient icon fate stands — this migration moves the data home, it does not answer that question.

Visit lines that the VisitScene step grammar cannot carry (the scattered LINE_* groups, if any prove to be non-step lines) ride a `# Strings:` visit table instead of staying hardcoded — sim IOU rule: any behavior a director still hardcodes after the port is named debt (pm gap).
